title: Spontaneous nanoemulsification for solubility enhancement of BCS class II and IV molecules
author: Alsufyani, Alqarni, et al.

steps.title: Screen excipient solubility for quercetin
steps.instruction: Determine the solubility of quercetin in a panel of candidate excipients and select the oil, surfactant, and co‑solvent with the highest solubility values for nanoemulsion preparation.

substeps.instruction: Prepare saturated quercetin solutions in each excipient (ethyl oleate, olive oil, coconut oil, Tween 20, Tween 80, isopropyl alcohol, propylene glycol).
Incubate mixtures under agitation until equilibrium is reached.
Measure the dissolved quercetin concentration (e.g., by UV‑Vis) and record the values:
Select ethyl oleate as the oil phase, Tween 80 as the surfactant, and propylene glycol as the co‑solvent because they provide the highest solubility for quercetin among the tested excipients.

steps.title: Dilute nanoemulsion and measure droplet size
steps.instruction: Prepare a diluted sample of the nanoemulsion and determine its droplet size distribution using photon correlation spectroscopy.

substeps.instruction: Pipette 0.1 mL of the freshly prepared nanoemulsion into a 50 mL volumetric flask.
Add distilled water up to the 50 mL mark.
Mix gently by inverting the flask several times to ensure homogeneity without introducing air bubbles.
Transfer an aliquot to a disposable cuvette and measure the droplet size with a Zetasizer 1000 HS (Malvern Instruments, UK) at 25 °C, using a scattering angle of 90°.

steps.title: Perform in vitro release in simulated intestinal fluid
steps.instruction: Assess the drug release from each nanoemulsion formulation in simulated intestinal fluid (pH 7.4) over 48 hours.

substeps.instruction: Prepare simulated intestinal fluid (SIF) adjusted to pH 7.4.
Introduce the nanoemulsion formulation (e.g., NE1, NE2, NE3, NE4, NE5) into the SIF under sink conditions.
Incubate the mixture at 37 °C with gentle shaking for a total of 48 hours.
At the end of the incubation, quantify the amount of quercetin released (e.g., by HPLC) and calculate the percentage released:

description: This method is a comprehensive analysis of the spontaneous emulsification method that generates nanoemulsions intended for oral administration. Nanoemulsions are easy to prepare by this method and require no significant energy contribution during preparation and thus scale up technology is easy. The methodology elucidates the principles behind the calculation and development of pseudo ternary phase diagrams. Most notably, it facilitates the selection of formulations from these phase diagrams to circumvent metastable formulations, ensuring minimal surfactant concentration was achieved in the shortest time frame. Before starting the phase diagram, one must have to select suitable excipients in which the drug shows maximum solubility to be in the desired solubility range which is essential for the formulation of nanoemulsion drug delivery system. On the basis of solubility study it was concluded that the solubility of quercetin in ethyl oleate was found to be favorable (Fig. 3) for the nanoemulsion preparation and was selected as oil phase.
